title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is a sextortion and extortion scheme in which AI-generated explicit video was one tool among several, not the point of entry. The gang's route in was a fake Facebook profile, and the recorded video call supplied the material that the AI-generated content was used to supplement. The AI output sat at the coercion stage of the operation, after contact had already been made and trust established.

The failure here is not a model asserting something false or a system running without a human check. It is impersonation and the fabrication of intimate material for leverage, combined with the ordinary infrastructure of fraud: mule accounts, a phone number tied to many complaints, and a run of activity reported as going back to 2023. Catching this kind of operation depends on complaint patterns and financial trails rather than on any check inside a model, because the harm is produced by people using a general capability deliberately.

What is not established is guilt. The reports describe arrests and police statements, and an FIR is not a conviction. The claim that the gang cheated hundreds of people and the figures attached to the seized accounts are police accounts of an ongoing investigation, not findings by a court.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student and three associates were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI using AI-generated explicit videos. Police said Md Faisal, 22, a second-year BCom student, and Md Amaan Tyagi, Md Hammad Tyagi and Md Faizaan Malik created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim during a video call on Sept 10, then demanded $50,000 and threatened to upload the footage and AI-made obscene videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on Sept 17, and the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints.

Police registered an FIR under the BNS and IT Act and arrested four gang members on Friday, while some associates remain absconding. Investigators said the gang had been active since 2023, cheated hundreds of people in India and abroad, and used mule accounts and AI sextortion videos. Their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore.
